newsitem.title: HAITI: Keep U.N. force in Haiti four extra months - U.S..
newsitem.headline: Keep U.N. force in Haiti four extra months - U.S..

text.p: The United States supports keeping U.N. peacekeepers in Haiti four months past a July 31 deadline for their withdrawal, the U.S. ambassador to the United Nations said on Monday.
"The U.S. strongly supports President (Rene) Preval's request for a mandate extension of four more months," Ambassador Bill Richardson said after meeting Preval at the national palace.
Richardson met former President Jean-Bertrand Aristide earlier in the day. Aristide has been a leading critic of Preval's economic reform plans.
"I had a good meeting with Aristide. He did tell me he supports the president and the president's view there should be support for four more months," he said.

Grass-roots groups calling themselves However They Go, They Go have threatened violence if the U.N. troops stay on. The same groups called sometimes violent demonstrations and strikes demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Rosny Smarth, who eventually stepped down last month.
Richardson said he was not aware of the movement. "I just need to get this mission extended," he said.

The envoy also visited parliament, an orphanage and a U.S. military road project. U.S. officials said his trip was important, as Richardson would lobby China and Russia, which are reluctant to support the peacekeeping extension in the U.N. Security Council.

Richardson said he was relatively optimistic the extension would be approved. U.N. officials said the U.N. force was likely to be scaled down from its current strength of 1,300 Pakistani and Canadian soldiers.
